cohort: Infants aged less than 6 months diagnosed with late-onset primary and secondary VKDB
finding: Secondary late VKDB was more common than the primary subtype, and late VKDB remains a serious disease in developing countries when vitamin K prophylaxis is not routinely used at birth.
mod_finding: The study found no significant difference in the mode of delivery (vaginal vs. cesarean) between infants with primary and secondary late vitamin K deficiency bleeding.
